messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: routing-decision anomaly spike detected (us-east-1 -> unexpected region fallback). Rule mismatch rate 18% over 5m window. Paging oncall: sara
sara: oncall here :wave: seeing lots of 502s and elevated p50/p95 for API key redwood-internal. Investigating logs now.
miguel: pinged the routing dashboards — looks like many requests in us-east are being routed to eu-west and picking a different model variant. Could be a policy change?
sara: agree. grabbing the last config snapshot and router logs. snippets: ```
[2026-03-15T12:01:04Z] routing_decision: {request_id: abc123, preferred_region: us-east-1, selected_region: eu-west-1, policy: "canary-variant"} 
[2026-03-15T12:01:04Z] model_variant: model-x-small (expected: model-x-opt)
```

deploy-bot: CONFIG-SERVICE: change applied to routing-policies/canary at 2026-03-15T11:58:22Z by eva (PR #3421).
eva: yup, that was my canary schema tweak. I renamed fallback_default -> default_fallback to make naming consistent for the rollout. Didn't think it would break back-compat. sorry.
miguel: ok that's likely it. router uses strict schema now; missing fallback_default key -> runtime falls back to service default which is to pick newest variant (model-x-small) and enable region_fallthrough. that triggers extra cross-region hops.
sara: we need mitigation now. Two immediate actions: 1) set a temporary routing override to force stable policy across regions, 2) patch config-service to map old field names back for current canary. i'll do (1).
sara: running admin override: ```bash
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \"https://control-plane/api/v1/admin/overrides\" -d '{"scope":"global","policy":"stable-prod"}'
```
sara: override applied at 2026-03-15T12:03:10Z :white_check_mark:
miguel: pushing a small mapping shim to config-service to accept fallback_default as alias for default_fallback. PR ready (reviewing)
deploy-bot: DEPLOY: config-service mapping-shim rolled out to canary at 2026-03-15T12:06:02Z (deploy id cfg-20260315-77).
sara: router metrics trending back — decision mismatch rate down to 1.2% and p95 back near baseline. still watching. :eyes:

raj: Customer-eng here — which customers saw impact and what to tell them? are requests failing, or just slowed?
sara: brief impact: 7 customers (mostly EU region) experienced increased latency (p95 up ~700ms) and sporadic 502s between 12:00 and 12:08 UTC while the bad variant and cross-region routing were in effect. No auth/data exposure; no token leaks.
raj: thx. i'll draft a note: explain root cause (schema rename caused back-compat break -> routing defaulted to newest variant and region fallthrough), mitigation (override + mapping shim), ETA for postmortem. want me to use P2 severity?
miguel: agree P2 — production impact limited/survivable, mitigated quickly. put follow-ups in postmortem.
sara: handing off to next oncall liz for monitoring + post-incident follow-ups. liz, short TL;DR: schema rename in PR #3421 removed alias; router interpreted missing key as default causing canary to route to wrong variant & trigger region fallthrough. mitigations executed: admin override applied, mapping shim deployed to config-service, metrics normalized.
liz: taking handoff :raised_hand: I'll keep the override in place until we ship a proper migration and add tests. assigning follow-ups: (1) migration script to map renamed fields, (2) add e2e for routing policy renames, (3) update rollout checklist to require compatibility flag.

sara: agreed. also open action: add a canary smoke that validates variant selection and region affinity.
miguel: adding a quick patch to the router to log explicit fallback reasoning (so we can trace when field is missing). PR coming.
eva: i'm owning the postmortem writeup and the compatibility tests. sorry again — didn't expect strict validation.
raj: i'll send a short customer note in the next 30m with apology + impact window + mitigations. cc: legal/security if needed.
sara: incident timer: total impact window ~8 minutes (12:00–12:08 UTC). no ongoing customer-facing errors.
incident-bot: Incident resolved, pager cleared at 2026-03-15T12:10:15Z.
liz: good job team. follow-ups: I'll create a concise incident card and schedule a 1hr postmortem for tomorrow. :thumbsup:
